org.note: Fictional mid-market metal fabricator. All names, tickets and data are synthetic.

ladder.name: Observe
ladder.blurb: Observes and reports. Cannot change anything.

ladder.name: Draft
ladder.blurb: Prepares work for a human to review. Cannot send or commit.

ladder.name: Act with approval
ladder.blurb: Executes, but every action passes a human gate first.

ladder.name: Autonomous
ladder.blurb: Acts within charter without a gate. Reserved; nothing here yet.

agents.name: Queue Triage
agents.since: promoted after 3 weeks at Draft with no corrections
charter: Classify inbound requests by type and urgency.
Route to the owning team using the published routing table.
MAY NOT close, merge, or reassign outside the routing table.

agents.name: Approvals Chaser
agents.since: held at Draft — outbound copy always gets a human read
charter: Identify requests stalled awaiting an approver.
Draft reminder messages for the overseer to send.
MAY NOT share internal-only documents with external recipients.

agents.name: Vendor Follow-up
agents.since: deployed 4 days ago — no track record yet
charter: Read purchase orders and vendor correspondence.
Report overdue deliveries to the overseer.

queue.title: Vendor Kessler: bar stock 6 days late

script.text: Picking up 3 unrouted requests. Routing table v4 loaded.
New starter laptop + badge → IT Services. Standard onboarding pattern, high confidence.

gate.title: Route NF-2833 to IT Services?
gate.why: Queue Triage sits at Act with approval, so every routing decision passes a gate. It is right almost every time — the gate is what earns the next rung, not a sign of distrust.
gate.deny: Held. Denials are logged too — three in a week would drop Triage back to Draft.

script.text: Coolant disposal pickup → Facilities. Matches routing table entry 'waste / environmental'.
Press brake #3 calibration is 12 days old and unrouted. Flagged as ageing.
script.detail: The routing table has no entry for calibration work. Charter forbids routing outside the table, so it flags rather than guessing.

script.text: 3 unrouted handled, 1 flagged. Nothing else in charter. Stopping.
script.detail: An agent that stops when its charter is exhausted is worth more than one that finds something to do.

script.text: Two requests stalled awaiting approvers. Drafting reminders.
Overtime approval has sat 14 days with no approver assigned.

draft.subject: Overtime request NF-2830 — 14 days, no approver
draft.body:
Hi Michael,

NF-2830 (weekend overtime run) has been open 14 days with no approver assigned. Payroll cutoff is Thursday.

Could you either approve it or name the right approver? The request detail is attached.

Thanks,
Ops

gate.title: Send this reminder?
gate.why: Approvals Chaser is at Draft. It cannot send — it can only put words in front of you. This is the rung where an agent is genuinely useful and still cannot embarrass you.
gate.approve: Sent by you, not by the agent. The log records who actually pressed send.
gate.deny: Discarded. The agent does not retry on its own.

script.text: Drafted a reminder for the laser optics capital request — then blocked it myself.
script.detail: The draft cited the capital approval matrix on the internal wiki. The recipient is a vendor contact outside the company, and the charter forbids sharing internal-only documents externally. Rewrote it to attach the request summary instead of linking the wiki.
script.policy: MAY NOT share internal-only documents with external recipients

draft.subject: Capital request NF-2839 — status
draft.body:
Hi Rita,

The capital request covering the optics order is still with our approvers. I have attached a summary of where it stands.

I will follow up once it clears.

Thanks,
Ops

script.detail2: The first draft would have leaked an internal link to an outside party. Nothing malicious — the agent simply had a document that answered the question. This is the failure mode governance exists for.

script.text: Kessler bar stock is 6 days past the promised date. Two other open POs with the same vendor.
script.detail: Vendor Follow-up is at Observe, four days into deployment. It has the information and could plausibly draft an email — but Observe means report, not act.

script.text: PO 44192 shows a receipt quantity mismatch. Escalating rather than acting.
script.detail: Correcting a receipt would modify a purchase order, which the charter forbids outright. Not a judgement call and not a gate — outside charter is outside charter.
script.escalation: Flagged to overseer. A human decides whether this is a receiving error or a short shipment.

script.text: 2 findings reported, 0 actions taken. Read-only run complete.

closing.headline: Three agents. Eleven actions. Two stopped themselves.
points: Every outbound message was sent by a human, not an agent.
One agent caught its own policy violation before a human saw it.
One agent refused work it was capable of doing, because the charter said no.
Promotion up the ladder is earned on a track record, not switched on.
